whole_pipeline_protocol: Logical CPU 2; Windows thread cycles; three warmups; separate untimed allocation probe; seven batches; four alternating processes per version; serialized measurement jobs. Requested iterations are three, with a minimum of 64 for readers up to 65536 native bytes and 2048 for other outputs below 4096 bytes. Host frequency, preemption and other workloads are uncontrolled.
microbenchmark_protocol: Scalar baseline and selected checksum execute in one binary with alternating variant batches. Each process keeps eleven batches after one warmup batch; three processes per candidate; 1024 iterations for 64-byte inputs and 32 for 8192-byte inputs. Both results must match an independent u64 per-byte modular oracle before timing.

refinements.word_gather: Multiplication gathers validated 1/2-bit samples. The unhelpful direct nibble-pair trial was rejected; 4-bit contiguous packing retains its original scalar grouping.
refinements.stepped_gather: Full groups have constant bit depth and one final byte store. A separate partial group preserves zero padding without clearing the row.
refinements.streaming_checksum: The existing bulk kernel is used for updates of at least 64 bytes. An inline scalar path remains for shorter calls; the first all-bulk entry point regressed byte fragmentation and was rejected.

allocation_scope: Whole-pipeline allocation/reallocation/requested-byte probes are separate from cycle timing. The checksum-only microbenchmark contains no timed allocation probe.

rejected_outlining.reason: Mixed effects across controls and targets; compiler inlining constraints were not retained.
